mainEntity.name: How much does a Jaguar XJ 4.0 engine replacement cost in the UK?

acceptedAnswer.text: A rebuilt Jaguar XJ 4.0 engine typically costs between £3,200 and £5,200 for supply only, depending on whether it is the early AJ26 or revised AJ27 variant. Supply and fit packages generally add £1,200-£1,800 for specialist labour and diagnostics.

mainEntity.name: What are the common signs my Jaguar XJ 4.0 engine is failing?

acceptedAnswer.text: Rattle on startup points to timing chain tensioner failure. Excessive blue smoke on startup indicates valve stem seal degradation. For early 1996-1998 models, excessive oil consumption and low compression are classic signs of Nikasil bore scoring.

mainEntity.name: Is it worth replacing the engine in a classic Jaguar XJ 4.0?

acceptedAnswer.text: It depends on the vehicle's condition. With typical market values ranging from £1,500 to £6,000, a £3,200-£5,200 rebuilt engine may approach or exceed 60% of the vehicle's value. If the chassis, interior, and electronics remain in exceptional condition, replacement is a viable way to preserve a classic executive saloon.

mainEntity.name: Can I upgrade my early AJ26 engine to the later AJ27 specification?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, this is highly recommended. The AJ27 features steel cylinder liners that permanently solve the Nikasil bore scoring issue found in the AJ26. Most specialists will supply an AJ27-spec rebuilt engine for an AJ26 application, providing a permanent, reliable fix with upgraded timing components.

mainEntity.name: Does a replacement Jaguar XJ 4.0 engine need ECU coding?

acceptedAnswer.text: While the X300/X308 generation is less complex than modern Ingenium engines, professional installation is still required. The immobiliser system may need synchronisation with the replacement engine's ECU, and throttle body adaptation is often necessary after an engine swap.

historyTimeline.h2: Jaguar XJ 4.0 - Engine History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: When the Jaguar XJ 4.0 launched in 1996, it introduced Jaguar’s first all-new V8 engine, replacing the older inline-six and V12 units with a lighter, more compact, and highly refined powerplant that defined the X300 and X308 generations.

milestones.description: AJ26 introduced, 4.0L naturally aspirated V8, 284hp. Early units featured Nikasil cylinder bore linings, which proved vulnerable to high-sulphur UK fuel.
AJ27 introduced for the X308 facelift. Steel cylinder liners replaced Nikasil, permanently solving the bore scoring crisis while maintaining the 284-290hp output.
AJ27S (Supercharged) introduced for the XJR 4.0, delivering 370hp via an Eaton supercharger, establishing Jaguar’s modern high-performance ethos.

historyTimeline.closingNote: Every engine fitted to the Jaguar XJ 4.0 is covered below, with UK rebuilt pricing and known failure points specific to these classic V8 variants.

commonProblems.h2: Jaguar XJ 4.0 Engine Problems - Repair Cost vs Replacement
commonProblems.h3: The Jaguar XJ 4.0 reliability profile is defined by the transition from the early Nikasil-lined AJ26 to the steel-lined AJ27. While the AJ27 resolved the catastrophic bore scoring issues, both variants share vulnerabilities with plastic timing chain tensioners and cooling system components. Every rebuilt Jaguar XJ 4.0 engine supplied through EnginesMarket includes upgraded internal components specifically designed to address these original factory failure points, backed by a minimum 12-month unlimited mileage warranty.

problems.h4: Timing Chain Tensioner Failure - Why the Jaguar XJ 4.0 AJ-V8 Fails Prematurely
problems.rootCause: The original plastic timing chain tensioner shoes become brittle with heat cycles and oil contamination, then crack or shatter. Chain slack follows, skipping teeth on cam sprockets, leading to valve-to-piston contact.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Full timing chain set replacement with upgraded steel-caged tensioners, new guides, and cam sprockets.
repairOptions.longevity: 80k-100k miles. Only viable if engine has NO rattling or fault codes. Prevents catastrophic failure.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit of rebuilt engine with upgraded timing components, new gaskets, oil pump, bench tested before dispatch.
repairOptions.longevity: 100k+ miles expected. Includes 12-month unlimited mileage warranty. All known weak points addressed.

problems.vehicleValueCheck: A typical Jaguar XJ 4.0 of relevant age is worth £1,500-£6,000 [THIRD-PARTY]. In this value band, a reconditioned or rebuilt engine at £3,200-£5,200 may approach or exceed 60% of the vehicle's current market value. If the lowest viable replacement cost exceeds approximately 60% of the vehicle's current market value, evaluate scrap value before committing.
problems.recommendation: If you catch the rattle early and have no fault codes, preventative replacement at a specialist (£1,500-£2,200) is excellent value. Once the chain has slipped, we recommend going straight to a rebuilt engine. The labour overlap is significant, and the repaired engine still carries risk of hidden bottom end damage.
problems.cta: -> Compare rebuilt AJ27 engine prices for your Jaguar XJ 4.0

problems.h4: Nikasil Bore Scoring (AJ26 Specific) - The Early X300 Weakness
problems.rootCause: Early AJ26 engines featured Nikasil cylinder bore linings which proved highly vulnerable to high-sulphur UK fuel, leading to rapid bore scoring, loss of compression, and excessive oil consumption.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit of rebuilt engine with steel cylinder liners (AJ27 spec), new piston rings, upgraded oil pump, bench tested.
repairOptions.longevity: The only reliable long-term solution. Rebuilding an AJ26 block is not recommended due to the inherent Nikasil flaw.

problems.vehicleValueCheck: For an early X300 valued between £1,500 and £4,000, replacement cost frequently exceeds the vehicle's value. Evaluate scrap or part-ex value first unless the car holds significant classic or sentimental value.
problems.recommendation: If your X300 4.0 is consuming oil or showing low compression, do not waste money on temporary fixes. A full replacement with an AJ27-spec steel-lined rebuilt unit is the only way to permanently resolve the Nikasil vulnerability.
